segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Excuse me, I'm sorry to bother you, but would you have time to answer a few questions?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: What's it about?

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: We're doing some market research for a new television channel starting in two years' time.

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: OK, why not?

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Lovely, we'll just work through this form. And if we could start with some personal background information . . . B Sure.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Right, if I could just have your age . . .

segments.speaker: B 35.
segments.en: A Right, great.. .

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Right, great. And your job?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Systems analyst, but for the form I don't know whether it would count as professional or business or what.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: What do you think?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: OK, it's more like business.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Fine. And would you mind my asking about your salary? Or we can leave it blank.

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: No, I don't mind. It's £40,000 a year.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Thank you. Right... about your current watching habits . . . what would you say is your main reason for watching TV?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Well, at work I tend to read for information and what have you, so I'd say that with TV it probably just helps me relax and unwind.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Fine. And how many hours a day on average do you watch TV?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Not a lot really . . . I should say just over an hour.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: So what are the two main times of the day that you watch TV?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Well, a little around breakfast time and then it tends to be really late - eleven or even midnight - when I've finished work.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: And what sort of programmes do you go for?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Some news bulletins but I also really like to put my feet up with some of the old comedy shows.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Fine. And turning to the new channel... which type of programmes would you like to see more of?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Well, I certainly don't think we need any more factual programmes like news and documentaries. I think we need more about things like local information ... you know, providing a service for the community. And in the same vein, perhaps more for younger viewers .. . you know, good quality stuff.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Ah ha. And if you had to give the new directors some specific advice when they set up the channel, what advice would you give them?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: I think I'd advise them to pay a lot of attention to the quality of the actual broadcast, you know, the sound system. People are very fussy these days about that and in general I think they ought to do lots more of these kinds of interview, you know, talking with their potential customers.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Oh, I'm glad you think it's valuable!

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Certainly . . . yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Good. OK, this will be a commercial channel of course, but how often do you think it is tolerable to have adverts?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Well out of that list I'd say every quarter of an hour. 1 don't think we can complain about that, as long as they don't last for ten minutes each time!

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Quite. And . . . would you be willing to attend any of our special promotions for the new channel?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Yes, I'd be very happy to, as long as they're held here in my area.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: OK, I'll make a note of that. And finally, may we put you on our mailing list?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Well, I'd prefer not. .. except for the information about the promotion you mentioned.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Can I have your name and address?

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Of course . . . here's my card.

segments.speaker: A
segments.en: Oh, lovely... and thank you very much for your time and we look forward to seeing you.

segments.speaker: B
segments.en: Yes, indeed. Urn, thanks.
